{"number":2,"title":"Transparent rounded corners carry a dark ring","body":"## What happens today

round_corner with the transparent flag set, written out as PNG or WebP, draws a thin dark outline along every curved corner. The pixels on the curve stay fully opaque and have their colors scaled toward black. Over any page background the corner looks as if it were traced with a dark pencil. The opaque form of the filter, without the transparent flag, blends its edge cleanly into the fill color.

## What should happen

The curve is smoothed through the alpha channel. Pixels on the edge keep their original color and become partly transparent, so the picture fades into whatever is behind it with no outline. Output formats without alpha, such as JPEG, should still show the fill color in the corners.

## How to see it

Start the image server and open this path in the browser:

/unsafe/300x200/filters:round_corner(60,255,255,255,1):format(png)/example.jpg

Zoom into any corner of the picture. Today a dark ring follows the arc where the picture meets the background. After the fix the arc fades into the background with no ring. The same path with format(webp) in place of format(png) shows the same ring. The image file is example.jpg.

## Where it came from

from thumbor.ext.filters import _round_corner
from thumbor.filters import BaseFilter, filter_method


class Filter(BaseFilter):
    @filter_method(
        r"[\d]+(?:\|[\d]+)?",
        BaseFilter.PositiveNumber,
        BaseFilter.PositiveNumber,
        BaseFilter.PositiveNumber,
        BaseFilter.Boolean,
    )
    async def round_corner(
        self, radius, red, green, blue, transparent=False
    ):  # pylint: disable=too-many-positional-arguments
        width, height = self.engine.size
        radius_parts = radius.split("|")
        a_radius = int(radius_parts[0])
        b_radius = int(radius_parts[1]) if len(radius_parts) > 1 else a_radius

        if transparent:
            self.engine.enable_alpha()

        mode, data = self.engine.image_data_as_rgb()
        imgdata = _round_corner.apply(
            1,
            mode,
            a_radius,
            b_radius,
            red,
            green,
            blue,
            width,
            height,
            data,
            transparent,
        )
        self.engine.set_image_data(imgdata)

from thumbor.ext.filters import _round_corner


def test_transparent_round_corner_edge_is_not_opaque_and_dark():
    # Issue #2: with the transparent flag, edge pixels of a rounded corner
    # keep alpha 255 while their RGB is scaled toward black, which draws a
    # dark ring. A white fill on a white image must never leave an opaque
    # pixel that is darker than white.
    width, height = 100, 100
    data = bytes([255, 255, 255, 255]) * (width * height)

    out = _round_corner.apply(
        1, "RGBA", 20, 20, 255, 255, 255, width, height, data, 1
    )

    pixels = [tuple(out[i : i + 4]) for i in range(0, len(out), 4)]
    ring = [p for p in pixels if p[3] == 255 and p[:3] != (255, 255, 255)]
    assert ring == []

{"number":3,"title":"Resized GIF loses its transparent background","body":"## What happens today

Some GIF files use a palette and mark one palette entry as transparent. The sticker image in the course images folder is one of them. Its background is transparent, so the page shows through around the blue disc.

Ask the image server for that GIF at a new size. The GIF that comes back is fully opaque. The area that used to be transparent is now a solid black box around the sticker.

The same request with PNG output keeps the transparency. The problem needs a palette source, GIF output, and the PILLOW_PRESERVE_INDEXED_MODE setting on. That setting is on by default.

## What should happen

A resize must not change which pixels are transparent. The GIF that comes back carries a transparency index. The pixels that were transparent in the source are transparent in the output. A GIF with no transparency stays opaque. PNG output keeps its partial alpha.

## How to see it

Start the image server with the course configuration. Open this path in the browser:

/unsafe/240x160/sticker.gif

Today you see the sticker inside a solid black box. After the fix the box is gone and the browser's own background shows around the sticker. The Pillow engine handles this request, not gifsicle.

from io import BytesIO

from PIL import Image

from thumbor.config import Config
from thumbor.context import Context
from thumbor.engines.pil import Engine


def test_resized_gif_keeps_transparent_corner():
    # Issue #3: a palette GIF with a transparent palette entry loses its
    # transparency when resized and written back as GIF with
    # PILLOW_PRESERVE_INDEXED_MODE on. The corner must stay transparent.
    config = Config()
    config.PILLOW_PRESERVE_INDEXED_MODE = True
    context = Context(config=config)

    src = Image.new("P", (40, 40), 1)
    src.putpalette([255, 0, 0, 0, 0, 255] + [0, 0, 0] * 254)
    src.info["transparency"] = 0
    buf = BytesIO()
    src.save(buf, "GIF", transparency=0)

    engine = Engine(context)
    engine.load(buf.getvalue(), ".gif")
    engine.resize(20, 20)
    out = engine.read(".gif")

    result = Image.open(BytesIO(out)).convert("RGBA")
    assert result.getpixel((0, 0))[3] == 0

    # PILLOW_PRESERVE_INDEXED_MODE on must keep the transparent background.
    config = Config()
    config.PILLOW_PRESERVE_INDEXED_MODE = True
    context = Context(config=config)

    engine = Engine(context)
    engine.load(STICKER.read_bytes(), ".gif")

        width, height = self.size
        return float(new_height) * width / height

        width, height = self.size
        return float(new_width) * height / width

        self.focal_points = focal_points

        self.calls["cover"] += 1

    @property
    def resize_error_message(self):
        message = "The engine resize should have been called with %sx%s" % (
            self.target_width,
            self.target_height,
        )
        if not self.engine.calls["resize"]:
            return "%s, but was never called" % message

        last_resize = self.engine.calls["resize"][0]
        return "%s, but was called with %sx%s" % (
            message,
            last_resize["width"],
            last_resize["height"],
        )

    def has_resized_properly(self):
        if not self.target_width and not self.target_height:
            return True

        same_as_source = (
            self.target_width == self.source_width
            and self.target_height == self.source_height
        )
        orig_height = (
            self.target_width == self.source_width
            and self.target_height == "orig"
        )
        orig_width = (
            self.target_width == "orig"
            and self.target_height == self.source_height
        )
        orig_both = (
            self.target_width == "orig" and self.target_height == "orig"
        )

        if same_as_source or orig_height or orig_width or orig_both:
            return True

        ensure(self.engine.calls["resize"], lambda: self.resize_error_message)

        if not self.target_width:
            ensure(
                self.engine.calls["resize"][0]["width"]
                == float(self.source_width)
                * self.target_height
                / self.source_height,
                lambda: self.resize_error_message,
            )
            ensure(
                self.engine.calls["resize"][0]["height"] == self.target_height,
                lambda: self.resize_error_message,
            )
            return True

        if not self.target_height:
            ensure(
                self.engine.calls["resize"][0]["width"] == self.target_width,
                lambda: self.resize_error_message,
            )
            ensure(
                self.engine.calls["resize"][0]["height"]
                == float(self.source_height)
                * self.target_width
                / self.source_width,
                lambda: self.resize_error_message,
            )
            return True

        ensure(
            self.engine.calls["resize"][0]["width"]
            == (
                self.target_width == "orig"
                and self.source_width
                or self.target_width
            ),
            lambda: self.resize_error_message,
        )
        ensure(
            self.engine.calls["resize"][0]["height"]
            == (
                self.target_height == "orig"
                and self.source_height
                or self.target_height
            ),
            lambda: self.resize_error_message,
        )
        return True

    @property
    def crop_error_message(self):
        message = (
            "The engine crop should have been called with %dx%d %dx%d"
            % (
                self.crop_left,
                self.crop_top,
                self.crop_right,
                self.crop_bottom,
            )
        )
        if not self.engine.calls["crop"]:
            return "%s, but was never called" % message

        last_crop = self.engine.calls["crop"][0]
        return "%s, but was called with %dx%d %dx%d" % (
            message,
            last_crop["left"],
            last_crop["top"],
            last_crop["right"],
            last_crop["bottom"],
        )

    def has_cropped_properly(self):
        if self.crop_left is None:
            ensure(
                not self.engine.calls["crop"],
                lambda: (
                    "The engine crop should NOT have been called but "
                    "was with %(left)dx%(top)d %(right)dx%(bottom)d"
                    % (self.engine.calls["crop"][0])
                ),
            )
            return True
        ensure(self.engine.calls["crop"], lambda: self.crop_error_message)
        ensure(
            (self.engine.calls["crop"][0]["left"] == self.crop_left),
            lambda: self.crop_error_message,
        )

        ensure(
            (self.engine.calls["crop"][0]["top"] == self.crop_top),
            lambda: self.crop_error_message,
        )

        ensure(
            (self.engine.calls["crop"][0]["right"] == self.crop_right),
            lambda: self.crop_error_message,
        )

        ensure(
            (self.engine.calls["crop"][0]["bottom"] == self.crop_bottom),
            lambda: self.crop_error_message,
        )

        return True

from tests.base import TestCase
from tests.fixtures.transformer_test_data import TestData
from thumbor.transformer import Transformer


class AutoCropMinimumSizeTestCase(TestCase):
    def test_auto_crop_never_produces_an_empty_crop(self):
        # Issue #4: a 1x1 source resized to 50x25 rounds the crop height
        # to 0, so the engine gets an empty crop and returns a blank image.
        data = TestData(
            source_width=1,
            source_height=1,
            target_width=50,
            target_height=25,
            halign="center",
            valign="middle",
            focal_points=[],
            crop_left=None,
            crop_top=None,
            crop_right=None,
            crop_bottom=None,
        )
        ctx = data.to_context()
        engine = ctx.modules.engine
        trans = Transformer(ctx)

        trans._calculate_target_dimensions()
        trans.adjust_focal_points()
        trans.auto_crop()

        assert engine.calls["crop"], "auto_crop should call the engine crop"
        crop = engine.calls["crop"][0]
        assert crop["right"] > crop["left"]
        assert crop["bottom"] > crop["top"]

from tests.base import TestCase
from tests.fixtures.transformer_test_data import TestData
from thumbor.transformer import Transformer


class AutoCropMinimumSizeTestCase(TestCase):
    def test_auto_crop_never_produces_an_empty_crop(self):
        # Issue #4: a 1x1 source resized to 50x25 rounds the crop height
        # to 0, so the engine gets an empty crop and returns a blank image.
        data = TestData(
            source_width=1,
            source_height=1,
            target_width=50,
            target_height=25,
            halign="center",
            valign="middle",
            focal_points=[],
            crop_left=None,
            crop_top=None,
            crop_right=None,
            crop_bottom=None,
        )
        ctx = data.to_context()
        engine = ctx.modules.engine
        trans = Transformer(ctx)

        trans._calculate_target_dimensions()
        trans.adjust_focal_points()
        trans.auto_crop()

        assert engine.calls["crop"], "auto_crop should call the engine crop"
        crop = engine.calls["crop"][0]
        assert crop["right"] > crop["left"]
        assert crop["bottom"] > crop["top"]

    def test_fit_in_1x1_of_wide_source_resizes_to_1x1(self):
        # Issue #4: /unsafe/fit-in/1x1/940x2.png rounds the resized height
        # of 940x2 down to 0 and the engine rejects it.
        data = TestData(
            source_width=940,
            source_height=2,
            target_width=1,
            target_height=1,
            halign="center",
            valign="middle",
            focal_points=[],
            crop_left=None,
            crop_top=None,
            crop_right=None,
            crop_bottom=None,
            fit_in=True,
        )
        ctx = data.to_context()
        engine = ctx.modules.engine
        trans = Transformer(ctx)

        trans._calculate_target_dimensions()
        trans.adjust_focal_points()
        trans.fit_in_resize()

        assert engine.calls["resize"] == [{"width": 1, "height": 1}]

    def test_fit_in_width_only_of_wide_source_resizes_to_100x1(self):
        # Issue #4: /unsafe/fit-in/100x0/940x2.png asks for a width only.
        # The resize must keep at least 1 pixel on every side.
        data = TestData(
            source_width=940,
            source_height=2,
            target_width=100,
            target_height=0,
            halign="center",
            valign="middle",
            focal_points=[],
            crop_left=None,
            crop_top=None,
            crop_right=None,
            crop_bottom=None,
            fit_in=True,
        )
        ctx = data.to_context()
        engine = ctx.modules.engine
        trans = Transformer(ctx)

        trans._calculate_target_dimensions()
        trans.adjust_focal_points()
        trans.fit_in_resize()

        assert engine.calls["resize"] == [{"width": 100, "height": 1}]
